title: Extending Applications Safely and Efficiently
problem: Applications require mechanisms to safely load and execute dynamic extensions or plugins at runtime, but existing approaches either compromise security through unrestricted code execution or incur significant performance overhead through validation and isolation.
motivation: Safe application extensibility is essential for plugin architectures, JIT compilation, and modular systems, and requires balancing strong safety guarantees with minimal runtime performance cost.
method: Instead of forcing a choice between unsafe unrestricted code execution or slow heavy isolation, the system assigns capabilities to each extension—specific access to the memory regions and system features it's allowed to use. Before executing dynamically loaded code, the system verifies it respects these constraints, catching unsafe operations upfront rather than repeatedly at runtime. This lightweight verification and control approach avoids the overhead of virtual machines or heavyweight sandboxes, letting extensions run at nearly native speed while still being confined.
key_novelty: A system that runs dynamic extensions safely at full speed by controlling what each one can access and verifying code before it executes, without virtualization.
contributions: System architecture for safe dynamic code extension with formal safety guarantees
Efficient verification and execution of runtime-loaded extensions
Mechanisms for capability-based access control in extension contexts
Performance evaluation demonstrating low overhead compared to baseline approaches
limitations: Specific technical mechanisms, evaluation methodology, and comparison baselines not discussed based on title alone.
